remarks: No tracked port carries a weather or closure entry this run. That is the correct state, not a gap: there is no active suspension anywhere in the tracked set, and the only live cyclone is more than a thousand kilometres from the nearest of them.

Dujuan is the single active system and it is not a supply-chain event for these ports. It strengthened from a tropical depression to a tropical storm since the 15 September read and has closed to 1,039 km from Busan at its forecast closest approach, but the track runs north into open water east of Japan rather than toward the Yellow or East China Sea. Nothing crosses the 600 km threshold, so no threat rows are written.

Shanghai/Ningbo remains the heaviest queue in the tracked set at 1.34M TEU at anchorage and a queue-to-berth ratio of 2.14 on the 13 September snapshot, with SEKO reporting 7-8 day berth waits at Waigaoqiao and Yangshan. That is post-typhoon bunching plus the pre-Golden Week rush, not weather, so no port entry is created and the site’s own idle-berth flag is deliberately left unsuppressed.

Linerlytica has not published a snapshot past 13 September. The congestion window returned the same 16 dates as the previous run and every value matched what was already stored, so no new dates were added and the stored history is unchanged at 50 dates.
